brief.t: As of 2026-10-30, old-crop (2026/27) unfixed call **sales** are 70.0k contracts (-357 w/w, -1,540 over 8 weeks) and old-crop unfixed **purchases** 28.3k (-424 w/w). Against the same week of the last five seasons, sales are at the 67th percentile (avg 75.1k) and purchases at the 40th (avg 36.2k). Beyond this season, merchants hold 11.9k of new-crop sales and 39.7k of new-crop purchases.

Net old-crop on-call is +41,752 (mill side). In old-crop COT, producers/merchants/processors/users hold 105.4k long and 219.2k short (net -113,877, +18,370 w/w). Their long/short ratio of 0.48 sits at the 24th percentile of the last three years: **commercials hold relatively little long cover, so fixing the mill-side book is more likely to need buying in the market**. The net and the ratio matter more than gross longs, which include calendar-spread legs held by trade houses. On the other side, total unfixed purchases of 68.0k (+2,032 over 8 weeks) compare with 241.4k PMU shorts and 28.6k swap-dealer shorts — producer fixing is latent selling, whether it runs through PMU hedges or swap structures.
Front contract **December 2026** is 3.6 weeks from first notice, with 11.4k unfixed sales and 15.2k unfixed purchases against 142.8k open interest. Next: March 2027 with 29.4k unfixed sales.

Old-crop unfixed sales of 7.30m bales equal 16% of USDA's 2026/27 world trade forecast (44.7m, October 2026). USDA sees Brazil exporting 16.0m bales vs the US 12.3m. US export sales (week of 2026-10-29): 4.39m running bales unshipped, China 7%.

Managed money is net long 56.2k (-10,276 w/w; 3-yr COT index 73). Spec length is elevated; with commercials light on long cover, mill fixing could still add buying, but a long spec book can also liquidate.
